turns.answer_text: If I unexpectedly had that extra amount of money, I would compare several possible uses before deciding what I wanted it to accomplish.
For planning software I care about offline access and simplicity; I would switch if shared reminders became a regular need, but not for search alone.
At a shared meal I scan the room before deciding what, if anything, needs attention.
If my familiar route suddenly changed roads, I'd first think detour or traffic and check the map rather than assume danger.
With a new planning app I would try it for a day before deciding whether to switch, but that trial itself does not tell you what factors would make me keep it.
An extra month of living costs would go into an emergency reserve.
If promised help for a move ran long, whether my friend would be left in a bind before a deadline would matter most; if not, I would protect my planned personal time.
On a familiar route deviation I'd check the map before deciding what the deviation meant; I haven't said what meaning I'd give it.
At a shared meal I first notice practical unmet things such as someone waiting for a seat or food.
If a friend said covering all the meal ingredients was too much, I'd ask their budget and either split the cost or simplify the meal.
With extra money I would think through the options before deciding what I wanted the money to do for me.
At a shared meal I look around first before deciding what deserves my attention; I haven't said what tends to catch it.
